title: KV cache PR mini-lab personal notes
content:
Context:
- PR #4827 modifies KV cache eviction heuristics and adds a tiny LRU-ish layer to keep short prefixes hot. Goal: reduce repeated attention recomputation for common prefixes while preserving steady-state memory.
- Reviewer: Marco. I want a short personal runbook to validate behavior, collect microbenchmarks, and propose low-friction followups.

Top-level questions to answer before merging:
1) Correctness: any race conditions when multiple async requests touch same cache key?
2) Memory: worst-case resident memory with pathological request stream (long-tail prompts + many unique prefixes).
3) Perf: does this reduce p95/p99 latency for small prompts? impact on throughput (tokens/sec) under batching?
4) Operational: clear observability hooks and toggles for safe rollback.

Quick summary of changes in this PR (my reading):
- adds prefix_hotness counter + decay step in cache manager
- eviction now considers hotness*sequence_len instead of only last_access_ts
- small refactor extracting cache key normalization into Cache::normalize_key() -> potential compatibility cut
- test coverage: unit tests for normalize_key but missing concurrent access tests and integration regression on batching loop

Immediate manual validation steps (local sandbox):
- Build and run small stress harness: cargo run --bin kv-stress -- --concurrency 16 --pattern common-prefixes
- Shell snippet: 
  for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello world prefix'$RANDOM'","max_tokens":8}' >/dev/null; done
- Observe memory (smem/top) and watch cache size via /debug/cache endpoint.

Microbenchmarks to collect (use bench harness):
- Baseline (main before PR) vs this branch, same hardware (local A100 dev), 3 runs each:
  * single-client low-traffic: 10 concurrent short requests (<=16 tokens) for 5m -> measure p50/p95/p99 latency + tokens/sec
  * bursty traffic: 200 qps 1s bursts, 5s idle, 10 cycles -> measure tail latency and failure rate
  * long-context mix: 30% long (>1024 tokens), 70% short -> measure memory spike and GC / eviction churn
- Export metrics to csv for quick plotting (script: tools/bench/export_csv.sh).

Test matrix additions (unit / integration ideas):
- Unit: two-threaded access to Cache::put/get with synthetic time advancement to prove no double-free or stale indexes. (Mock time helper exists in tests/utils/time_ctrl.rs)
- Integration: small harness that spins up the full runtime with batching enabled (cfg=batched) and runs repeated short prompts for same prefix -> assert that expensive attention recompute counter (prometheus:attention_recomputes_total) does not increase linearly.
- Regression: ensure normalize_key() edgecases: non-utf8 tokenization boundary, trailing whitespace, and special tokens.

Observability / metrics to add before merge (or as follow-up but gated):
- export cache_hotness_percentile (p50/p95 of hotness)
- metric for number of cache evictions per minute, and eviction_reason label (age|memory|hotness)
- crucial: tag per-model cache metrics (model=...)
- debug endpoint: /debug/cache/sample to return top-10 hot keys (hashed) and their hotness counters -> redact actual prompt text

Potential risk areas and mitigations:
- Compatibility: Cache::normalize_key change could break persisted on-disk caches or keys shared across instances. Mitigate: maintain compatibility flag and migration path, or keep old code behind feature flag.
- Latency regressions under high-concurrency due to extra atomic increments on hotness counters. Mitigation: use sharded counters (fast path) or sample-only updates (e.g., 1-in-10 requests).
- Memory blowup if many unique short prefixes are treated as hot. Mitigation: clamp hotness to reserve fraction of total cache size; prefer TTL-based eviction if hotness density exceeds threshold.

Small refactors to propose as separate PRs (smaller, easy review):
- Extract CacheKeyHasher trait and add tests for stable hashing across versions (helps in future rolling upgrades).
- Move normalize_key() docs into code comment + add table of examples in unit tests.
- Replace global atomic counter with per-shard counters behind a small bench to show perf improvement.

Questions for Marco (to put in PR review comments):
- Did you consider sampling hotness updates instead of updating on every get()? Can we add a flag to control update frequency?
- For normalize_key(), do we need compatibility tests for persisted checkpoints? which teams rely on stable keys?
- Are there any downstream consumers (dedicated private deployments) that depend on exact key format? (cc @Ananya for infra visibility)

Next steps (my TODO list):
- [ ] Run the 3 microbench modes and attach csvs to PR
- [ ] Add concurrent access unit test with time_ctrl
- [ ] Add eviction_reason metric and a short note in CHANGELOG
- [ ] Propose follow-up PR to shard counters if perf regresses
- [ ] Leave inline comments on PR pointing to specific lines where I think a lock-free path might help (Cache::get hot path)

Notes-to-self (random):
- If we see significant p99 regression, flip to old behavior via feature toggle and schedule a quick rollout. Keep an eye on Canary group 1 latency for first 30m after deploy.
- Remember: small memory savings are not worth p99 regressions. Prioritize safety and clear rollback.

End of notes.

Scratch history:
- initial quick read 2025-11-02, flagged missing tests
- chatted with Marco in slack on 2025-11-04 (thread: linked_artifacts[2])
- promised to run microbench on 2025-11-10 but delayed, rescheduled to 2026-02-12
- updated notes with experiments on 2026-02-14
